clean_description: Homegoing follows the lives of two half-sisters, Effia and Esi, born in 18th-century Ghana. While Effia marries an Englishman and lives in comfort, Esi is captured and sold into slavery, leading to a narrative that spans eight generations and explores the impact of slavery on both sides of the Atlantic. The novel examines the legacy of trauma and memory within families and communities affected by slavery.
setting: Ghana and the United States across centuries
